what_worked: Mean-vs-median callout on slide 3 and cumulative concentration curve on slide 5 are genuinely useful analytical moments.
fix_next: Strip the promotional fund-pitch wrapper and interrogate the data—why 216 zero-revenue companies, category median differences, provider-revenue efficiency.
verdict: Polished pitch deck that describes data without genuinely analyzing it; several fabricated or misattributed figures.
factual_error_detail: Slide 1/2: $161.7M ARR implies $13.47M MRR, but total 30-day revenue is $15.6M—unexplained gap. Slide 2: $334.0M cumulative lifetime revenue has no basis in the dataset. Slide 5: 26.5% 'single largest position' conflates the anonymous-cohort revenue share with a single company. Slide 6: 74% outside US uses 1,000 denominator but 241 rows have missing country (correct base is 759 known). Slide 12: '26% operates outside the US' contradicts slide 6's own 74% claim—internally inconsistent.

evidence.insight: Only two real analytical moves: slide 3 mean/median gap and slide 5 power-law curve. No exploration of zero-revenue companies (216), no category-median comparison, no provider-revenue efficiency, no TLD or audience-type analysis. Insights describe rather than interrogate.
evidence.narrative: Coherent LP-update arc from overview through risk to fundraising ask. Sequence is purposeful but the thesis (diversification + breakouts) is asserted, never stress-tested. The narrative never challenges its own premise or surfaces uncomfortable findings.
evidence.framing: Creative VC-fund persona but obscures the student data-story assignment. A cold reader cannot tell this is coursework. Scope/limitations partially addressed on slides 11-12 but missingness rates are understated and the 'coming soon' methodology slide is filler that displaces real analysis.
evidence.accuracy: Category counts on slide 4 match reference. Provider shares on slide 8 approximately correct by company count. However, $334M lifetime revenue is fabricated, 26.5% single-position claim misreads anonymous cohort data, 74% outside-US ignores 241 missing country values, and the MRR figure doesn't reconcile with total 30-day revenue. Slide 12 internally contradicts slide 6 on US/non-US split.
evidence.visual: Consistent navy/gold/teal palette, clean typography, good hierarchy. Bar charts on slides 4 and 6 are well-labeled. Cumulative curve on slide 5 is effective. Pie chart on slide 8 is acceptable. Some slides are KPI-card walls with no real visualization (slides 2, 7, 9). Visual sameness across the deck.
evidence.ai_slop: Pervasive pitch-deck language: 'high-velocity startups,' 'real-time visibility — by design,' 'punching well above its weight,' 'the outlier we underwrote for,' 'built to withstand the power law.' Fictional fund wrapper with fake contact info, Fund II raise, and $150M target displaces analytical substance. Slide 11 is pure filler.

change_reason: Lowered insight from 5→4.5 (data described not interrogated, zero-revenue and category-median analyses absent), narrative from 6.5→6.0 (thesis never challenged, promotional arc substitutes for analytical tension), framing from 5.5→5.0 (fictional fund obscures assignment context, missingness understated), accuracy from 5.5→4.5 (five factual errors including fabricated $334M figure and internal contradiction on US share). Visual and bonus unchanged.
